Crucial

/KROO-shul/ — stress on KROO · adjective

Hear It

No recording available for this word.

What It Means

Crucial describes something extremely important, especially because a great deal depends on it.

Bringing the spare key turned out to be a crucial decision.

Worked Example

The goalkeeper's crucial save in the final seconds of the match kept his team from losing.

Latin crux (the point where paths cross / the decisive point) + -ial = characteristic of the crux. A crucial save is one that determines the outcome of the match — it's the decisive moment where everything hinges. This is different from a 'good save'; it's good AND its outcome is decisive.

How Crucial Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

critical

critical: vitally important at a decisive moment

essential

essential: absolutely necessary; cannot be left out

pivotal

pivotal: the point everything else turns on

Antonyms

trivial

trivial: of little value or importance

insignificant

insignificant: too minor to affect the outcome

How Strong Is It? — relevant → important → essential → crucial

relevant vs. crucial

relevant vs. crucial: A relevant detail relates to the problem, but a crucial detail can decide the entire outcome.

important vs. crucial

important vs. crucial: Important means it matters, while crucial means the whole result depends on it.

essential vs. crucial

essential vs. crucial: Essential means it cannot be left out, but crucial adds urgency — this is the decisive point where everything is won or lost.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — cruc(i)

Root — cruc(i): cross; the decisive point where paths meet (Latin crux, crucis) (Latin)

Suffix — -ial

Suffix — -ial: characteristic of; relating to (Latin (-alis))

Put it together

Put it together: The Latin root crux means 'cross' — pictured as the decisive point where two paths meet — and -ial means 'characteristic of.' So crucial means 'characteristic of the decisive point': so important that the outcome hinges on it.

Use the root in a new word: crux

Use the root in a new word: crux: The crux of the debate was whether students should be allowed to grade their own homework.

Word Choice

formal

Use crucial to describe something that is the decisive factor — the moment or choice where the outcome is determined. It's stronger than 'important' because it carries the sense of a crossing point, a make-or-break moment. When stakes are high and one thing determines the direction, crucial is your word.
